label: models/fw_pipejunction.mdl: two pipes meeting at a flanged elbow, bolted

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_hgun.mdl, models/w_suit.mdl, models/w_oxygen.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked B, B, D, D where the asset was C, A, A, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The outline matches the brief's words in all ten views: a vertical pipe rising from a flanged elbow, with a second pipe running off the elbow at a flanged joint. The elbow is a clear bend, and the two pipes meet at it as the brief asks. No part sticks out or is missing.

M2.reason: The brief gives no size for the pipe junction, so there is no figure to measure against (sizeAsked null, sizeOff null). The 49.5 x 18.1 x 56 build is a plausible pipe-junction size and nothing in the brief is contradicted.

M3.reason: Parts the brief implies, checked down to the small ones: two pipes (vertical and horizontal), the flanged elbow, flange rings at the top joint, the elbow joint and the horizontal joint, bolts on the flange rims (visible in TOP, BACK and FRONT-LEFT), and the two base plates. All are present and in place. The pipe ends look coarsely faceted (octagonal in TOP and FRONT-LEFT), but the brief sets no side count, so this is not charged.

M4.reason: Rust-brown flanges and elbow over blue-grey, rust-mottled pipes read as rusted steel, as the brief's worn metal asks. The colours are consistent across all views.

M5.reason: The rust mottling, the flange rims and the bolt tabs are in their places, and the wear is at a sharpness that suits the prop. Nothing is added that is wrong.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the rule. In the line-up the judges picked B, B, D, D, and never the asset (C, A, A, C), so it passed as one of the game's.

M7.reason: Upright, with the vertical pipe pointing up and the foot plate under it. It stands on its foot plate as the line-up shows, with the front flange facing the viewer.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors and 412 triangles is under the 476 allowed (twice the median of 238, which is more than the third quartile of 291). But the elbow's mouth in the front and below views shows a dark hollow with no visible inner wall, while the back view shows a closed face. That reads as an open or inverted surface a player can see, so this is held at 1.
